arxiv-2102-13079.title: Quantization Algorithms for Random Fourier Features
arxiv-2102-13079.creator: Xiaoyun Li, Ping Li
arxiv-2102-13079.description: Abstract The method of random projection (RP) is the standard technique in machine learning and many other areas, for dimensionality reduction, approximate near neighbor search, compressed sensing, etc. Basically, RP provides a simple and effective scheme for approximating pairwise inner products and Euclidean distances in massive data.

arxiv-2106-07162.title: Goal-Aware Neural SAT Solver
arxiv-2106-07162.creator: Emils Ozolins, Karlis Freivalds, Andis Draguns, Eliza Gaile, Ronalds Zakovskis, Sergejs Kozlovics
arxiv-2106-07162.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Emils Ozolins, Karlis Freivalds, Andis Draguns, Eliza Gaile, Ronalds Zakovskis, Sergejs Kozlovics. Modern neural networks obtain information about the problem and calculate the output solely from the input values. We argue that it is not always optimal, and the network’s performance can be significantly improved by augmenting it with a query mechanism that allows the network at run time to make several solution trials and get feedback on the loss value on each trial.

arxiv-2110-03668.title: From classical to quantum stochastic processes
arxiv-2110-03668.creator: Gustavo Montes, Soham Biswas, Thomas Gorin
arxiv-2110-03668.description: Abstract In this paper for the first time, we construct quantum analogs starting from classical stochastic processes, by replacing random “which path” decisions with superpositions of all paths. This procedure typically leads to non-unitary quantum evolution, where coherences are continuously generated and destroyed. In spite of their transient nature, these coherences can change the scaling behavior of classical observables.

arxiv-2201-07799.title: The minimum number of some resolving sets for the Crystal Cubic Carbon C ​ C ​ C ​ ( n ) CCC(n) and the Layer Cycle Graph L ​ C ​ G ​ ( n , k ) LCG(n,k) Journal: –
arxiv-2201-07799.creator: Jia-Bao Liu, Ali Zafari
arxiv-2201-07799.description: Abstract The problem of determining resolving sets in graph theory has a long history, as it has many applications in chemistry, robot navigation, combinatorial optimization and utilization of the idea in pattern recognition and processing of images that also provide motivation for founding the theory. Especially, it is well known that these problems are NP hard.

arxiv-2303-07899.title: User Preferences of Spatio-Temporal Referencing Approaches For Immersive 3D Radar Charts Journal: arXiv.org cs.HC
arxiv-2303-07899.creator: Nico Reski, Aris Alissandrakis, Andreas Kerren
arxiv-2303-07899.description: Abstract The use of head-mounted display technologies for virtual reality experiences is inherently single-user-centred, allowing for the visual immersion of its user in the computer-generated environment. This isolates them from their physical surroundings, effectively preventing external visual information cues, such as the pointing and referral to an artifact by another user.

arxiv-2303-08120.title: Blind Video Deflickering by Neural Filtering with a Flawed Atlas
arxiv-2303-08120.creator: Chenyang Lei, Xuanchi Ren, Zhaoxiang Zhang, Qifeng Chen
arxiv-2303-08120.description: Abstract Many videos contain flickering artifacts; common causes of flicker include video processing algorithms, video generation algorithms, and capturing videos under specific situations. Prior work usually requires specific guidance such as the flickering frequency, manual annotations, or extra consistent videos to remove the flicker.

arxiv-2306-04640.title: ModuleFormer: Modularity Emerges from Mixture-of-Experts
arxiv-2306-04640.creator: Yikang Shen, Zheyu Zhang, Tianyou Cao, Shawn Tan, Zhenfang Chen, Chuang Gan
arxiv-2306-04640.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable results. But existing models are expensive to train and deploy, and it is also difficult to expand their knowledge beyond pre-training data without forgetting previous knowledge. This paper proposes a new neural network architecture, ModuleFormer , that leverages modularity to improve the efficiency and flexibility of large language models.

arxiv-2307-05769.title: Joint Machine-Transporter Scheduling for Multistage Jobs with Adjustable Computation Time
arxiv-2307-05769.creator: Koresh Khateri, Giovanni Beltrame
arxiv-2307-05769.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Koresh Khateri, Giovanni Beltrame. This paper presents a scalable solution with adjustable computation time for the joint problem of scheduling and assigning machines and transporters for missions that must be completed in a fixed order of operations across multiple stages. A battery-operated multi-robot system with a maximum travel range is employed as the transporter between stages and charging them is considered as an operation. Robots are assigned to a single job until its completion.

arxiv-2309-00669.title: Dark Matter Capture in Celestial Objects: Treatment Across Kinematic and Interaction Regimes
arxiv-2309-00669.creator: Juri Smirnov
arxiv-2309-00669.description: Abstract Signatures of dark matter in celestial objects have become of increasing interest due to their powerful detection prospects. To test any of these signatures, the fundamental quantity needed is the rate in which dark matter is captured by celestial objects.

arxiv-2402-03079.title: Simulating Atmospheric Processes in Earth System Models and Quantifying Uncertainties with Deep Learning Multi-Member and Stochastic Parameterizations
arxiv-2402-03079.creator: Gunnar Behrens, Tom Beucler, Fernando Iglesias-Suarez, Sungduk Yu, Pierre Gentine, Michael Pritchard, Mierk Schwabe, Veronika Eyring
arxiv-2402-03079.description: Abstract Deep learning is a powerful tool to represent subgrid processes in climate models, but many application cases have so far used idealized settings and deterministic approaches. Here, we develop stochastic parameterizations with calibrated uncertainty quantification to learn subgrid convective and turbulent processes and surface radiative fluxes of a superparameterization embedded in an Earth System Model (ESM).

arxiv-2405-19039.title: Heavy baryons in the relativized quark model with chromodynamics
arxiv-2405-19039.creator: Xin-Zhen Weng, Wei-Zhen Deng, Shi-Lin Zhu
arxiv-2405-19039.description: Abstract Following the work of Capstick and Isgur [ Phys. Rev. D 34, 2809 (1986) ], we systematically study the mass spectrum of the heavy baryons in the relativized quark potential model with chromodynamics. Besides the original Godfrey-Isgur (GI) model, we also adopt a modified GI model which replaces the linear confinement by a screened one.

arxiv-2408-01905.title: Enhanced Sensing by Geometric Tuning of YIG Spheres: Noise Reduction, Signal Amplification and Directional Magnetic Field Detection
arxiv-2408-01905.creator: Zheng Liu, Ding-hui Xu, Yi-jia Yang, and Chang-shui Yu
arxiv-2408-01905.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Zheng Liu, Ding-hui Xu, Yi-jia Yang, and Chang-shui Yu. Noise suppression and directional signal enhancement are essential challenges in detecting weak magnetic fields in cavity electrodynamics systems. Traditional schemes struggle to reduce magnonic probe noise but lack directional sensing capabilities. We exploit an innovative and intrinsic squeezing mechanism by leveraging the geometric configuration of an anisotropic ellipsoidal yttrium iron garnet (YIG) sphere and its interaction with internal demagnetization fields.

arxiv-2505-09376.title: AfforDance: Personalized AR Dance Learning System with Visual Affordance Conference: CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems; April 26, 2025; Yokohama, Japan CCS: Human-centered computing User interface design CCS: Human-centered computing Mixed / augmented reality
arxiv-2505-09376.creator: Hyunyoung Han, Jongwon Jang, Kitaeg Shim, Sang Ho Yoon
arxiv-2505-09376.description: Abstract . We propose AfforDance, an augmented reality (AR)-based dance learning system that generates personalized learning content and enhances learning through visual affordances. Our system converts user-selected dance videos into interactive learning experiences by integrating 3D reference avatars, audio synchronization, and adaptive visual cues that guide movement execution.

arxiv-2505-16310.title: Paired and Unpaired Image to Image Translation using Generative Adversarial Networks
arxiv-2505-16310.creator: Gaurav Kumar, Soham Satyadharma, Harpreet Singh
arxiv-2505-16310.description: Abstract Image-to-image translation is an active area of research in the field of Computer Vision, enabling the generation of new images with different styles, textures, or resolutions while preserving their characteristic properties. Recent architectures leverage Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) to transform input images from one domain to another.

pmc-10602928.title: Let's make it clear: systematic exploration of mitochondrial DNA– and RNA–protein complexes by complexome profiling
pmc-10602928.creator: Alisa Potter, Alfredo Cabrera-Orefice, Johannes N Spelbrink
pmc-10602928.description: Complexome profiling (CP) is a powerful tool for systematic investigation of protein interactors that has been primarily applied to study the composition and dynamics of mitochondrial protein complexes. Here, we further optimized this method to extend its application to survey mitochondrial DNA- and RNA-interacting protein complexes.

pmc-11375142.title: The effect of phosphorylation efficiency on the oncogenic properties of the protein E7 from high-risk HPV
pmc-11375142.creator: Madison Malone, Ava Maeyama, Naomi Ogden, Kayla N. Perry, Andrew Kramer, Caleb Bates, Camryn Marble, Ryan Orlando, Amy Rausch, Caleb Smeraldi, Connor Lowey, Bronson Fees, H. Jane Dyson, Michael Dorrell, Heidi Kast-Woelbern, Ariane L. Jansma
pmc-11375142.description: Highlights•The protein E7 from high-risk HPV is phosphorylated by the protein kinase CK2 to a greater degree compared to low-risk HPV, which could be a contributing factor to the oncogenic properties of high-risk HPV.•The presence of valine residues in the CK2 recognition sequence of E7 are prevalent in the most clinically relevant low-risk serotypes of HPV.

pmc-11404451.title: Identification of leader–trailer helices of precursor ribosomal RNA in all phyla of bacteria and archaea
pmc-11404451.creator: Bryan T Gemler, Benjamin R Warner, Ralf Bundschuh, Kurt Fredrick
pmc-11404451.description: Ribosomal RNAs are transcribed as part of larger precursor molecules. In Escherichia coli, complementary RNA segments flank each rRNA and form long leader–trailer (LT) helices, which are crucial for subunit biogenesis in the cell. A previous study of 15 representative species suggested that most but not all prokaryotes contain LT helices.

pmc-11418304.title: Exploring the Correlation Between Hypoxia, HIF1A Variants, and Breast Cancer in Different Ethnicities, and Bangladeshi Women: Through ELISA and Integrative Multi-Omics Analysis
pmc-11418304.creator: Md. Shihabul Islam, Jesmin
pmc-11418304.description: Background:Hypoxia, a condition where there is a lack of oxygen, is known to play a role in cancer progression.Objective:This study investigates the correlation between HIF1A gene-altered expression and hypoxia in Bangladeshi breast cancer (BC) cases and TCGA_BC datasets.Design:This case-control study compares BC cases to healthy controls to understand the relationship between gene changes and cancer.

pmc-12604111.creator: Kate Browne, Juan Garcia Burgos, Eva Jirsová, Robin Ruepp, Gernot Bonkat, Shlomo Vinker, Walter Marrocco, Tiago Villanueva
pmc-12604111.description: ghts into the clinical uncertainty surrounding the management of male cystitis and highlights a tendency towards empirical and prolonged fluoroquinolone use for the treatment of mUTIs. pmc-12700422.title: Understanding the influence of power dynamics in intersectoral collaboration: A realist evaluation in Assam, India
pmc-12700422.creator: Praveenkumar Aivalli, Brynne Gilmore, Prashanth Nuggehalli Srinivas, Aoife De Brún
pmc-12700422.description: Intersectoral Collaboration (ISC) involves multiple sectors working together to tackle complex challenges that no single sector can address alone. In global health, where interconnected issues demand holistic approaches, ISC aligns goals and resources to enhance effectiveness and equity. However, power dynamics within and between sectors can either foster synergy or create tensions, shaping ISC outcomes.

pmc-13433028.title: Signal detection and analysis of adverse events associated with sevelamer post-marketing based on the FAERS database
pmc-13433028.creator: Junxia Cao, Na Yang, Cheng Huang
pmc-13433028.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This study aimed to evaluate adverse events (AEs) associated with sevelamer through data mining of the US FDA Adverse Event Reporting System, identify potential drug-related AEs, and provide guidance for clinical medication safety. AE reports related to sevelamer from the first quarter of 2004 to the second quarter of 2025 were extracted from the US FDA Adverse Event Reporting System database, classified by preferred term (PT) and system organ class, and risk signals were analyzed.

pmc-13493282.title: Assessment of AI-based cephalometric landmark recognition on lateral cephalometric radiographs
pmc-13493282.creator: Amani Idres, Mohamed Osman, Ahmed Ghoneima
pmc-13493282.description: BackgroundArtificial intelligence (AI) strategies have been proposed for automatic landmark recognition applications with the expectation of simplifying and improving cephalometric analysis through accurate and consistent landmarks identification. The aim of the current study was to evaluate the accuracy and reliability of AI in identifying cephalometric landmarks for orthodontics cephalometric tracing.

pmc-13589479.title: Emerging role of GLP-1 mono, dual, and triple agonists in the management of MASH-related fibrosis
pmc-13589479.creator: Federica Tavaglione, Rohit Loomba
pmc-13589479.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). SummaryRecent therapeutic advances have resulted in US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval of the first pharmacological agents—resmetirom and semaglutide—for advanced metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) without cirrhosis, reshaping the therapeutic landscape of the disease. Within this evolving framework, incretin-based pharmacotherapies—including glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists and their dual and triple combinations with glucose-dependent insulinotropic peptide (GIP) and/or glucagon receptor agonists—have emerged as promising options, particularly for individuals with coexisting obesity or type 2 diabetes.
